Each item has a Criterion: % of sales (value = % × sales), {days} (DSO/DPO: Δ of the level × days/30 — A/R on sales, A/P on costs), Lead/Lag (% × sales of month m−lag; +lag/−lead, e.g. Deposits Applied), or Manual (you type/paste). Columns: «before» = deposits (Received/Applied); «same month» = direct cash; «+1m» = credit/A-R. E.g. December: raise 3m/2m before (the 20th–31st sale comes in during October) and drop «+1m» to 0. Replaces and supersedes the NRR·Flex·Stay·Credit boxes.
cfCriteria.activeModelNote: With the model ACTIVE, these rules calculate Deposits Received/Applied, A/R, A/P, Christmas bonus and IVA in the Cash Flow Budget and the projected Balance Sheet. cfCriteria.fAguinaldoHelp: It accrues every month and is paid in full in the payment month.
cfCriteria.fApSameHelp: Suppliers: % paid in the same month (the rest the next one). You set it at 60/40.
cfCriteria.fCardIvaHelp: 2.5% withheld by the tax authority on card collections → an IVA credit balance usable the following month. It affects WC_TAX.
cfCriteria.fCardPctHelp: 70%. The tax authority withholds IVA and income tax on this amount. There is ONE SINGLE figure for the whole hotel: it applies to total operating collections, not line by line. A new profit centre (e.g. Private Bar) inherits this same %; giving it one of its own means changing the model, not adding a field here.
cfCriteria.fCardRentaHelp: 2.5% withheld for income tax on card collections → an annual credit balance (closes in December, settled in March). It affects WC_RENTTAX.
cfCriteria.fIvaRateHelp: 13% on sales (debit) and purchases (credit). The settlement is the difference, paid the following month.
cfCriteria.fOutsourcedHelp: If an outside firm invoices a payroll charge with IVA: payroll enters the A/P and IVA-credit base. Switch it off if payroll is handled in-house (no IVA).
cfCriteria.fRetentionHelp: % of the deposit received that is held back that month (cancellations/adjustments). It is released the following month → it affects the timing of WC_DEP_RECV. ⬇ The collection MIX and TIMING (formerly NRR/Flex/Stay/Credit + advance deposits) are now set in the collection timing matrix below.
cfCriteria.fServiceLagHelp: 1 = it is paid the month after it is collected. What is collected in one month is paid to the employees with this lag.
cfCriteria.fServiceRateHelp: The statutory 10% on F&B revenue (REV_FB). It is NOT hotel income: it is the employees' money (pass-through). It is COLLECTED with the sale (cash in) and PAID to the employees the following month (cash out). The float sits as a liability, 'F&B service charge payable' (WC_SERVICE). The F&B revenue in the P&L does NOT include this 10%. ⚠ The base is ONLY REV_FB: the Private Bar (dept 0121) came out of F&B and has its own line (REV_PRIVATE_BAR), so its sales carry no statutory service charge. That line is at zero today and moves no number; whether it should carry it is the owner's call.

setupCuenta.intro2: It is read-only and moves no number. The line comes from the same resolver the P&L engine uses, not from a copy: if it says one thing here, that is what the P&L does.

a_costo_de_planilla_por_departamento.deDonde: Opens the detail of accrued payroll by department, exactly as it lands in the P&L. It is informational: this box is not added on top, it is already inside the total P&L cost that the cash flow pays.

a_costo_devengado_del_mes.deDonde: The expense as the P&L recognizes it, before any payment criterion is applied. There is no cash here yet: this is what was consumed during the month.

a_hacienda_retencion_de_renta_al_salario.deDonde: The employee's income tax withholding. It is a different thing from the company's income tax and from the 2.5% withholding on card collections.

a_la_ccss_cotizacion_obrera_retenida.deDonde: The 10.67% withheld from the employee, which the hotel deposits with the CCSS along with the employer contribution. In the Summary the two travel on a single line.

aguinaldo_provision.deDonde: The Christmas bonus accrual: one twelfth of the taxable base, built up every month. PITFALL: this is accrual, not cash. The money does not go out month by month — it is paid in full in its own month. In the Summary the accrual is netted out of the payroll payment and the disbursement shows up only in December.

al_empleado_neto_en_la_mano.deDonde: The payroll deposit: the gross, already net of the two withholdings.

b2_a_donde_va_el_salario_bruto.deDonde: Splits that same gross wage across its three destinations, so it is visible that the gross is not paid to the employee in full.

b_del_bruto_a_la_neta_lo_que_recibe_el_e.deDonde: Separates what the hotel accrues from what the employee actually takes home. Everything subtracted in this block is a withholding: it comes out of the gross, it is not additional cost.

b_del_gasto_al_pago.deDonde: From accrual to cash: the month's expense is not all paid within the month. The schedule is the SAME one the indirect cash flow uses — there is no second payment model.

c_cargas_sociales_patronales_encima_del_.deDonde: Everything in this block is paid by the hotel ON TOP of the wage: it is not deducted from anyone, it is pure cost. It is the difference between what the employee sees on the pay stub and what the hotel actually spends.

c_como_se_reparte_el_pago.deDonde: The total payment is broken out into payroll and suppliers because the board reads them differently, even though both are paid on the same schedule.

cafeteria.deDonde: Staff meals. PITFALL: it does not come from a per-person per diem — it comes from the ALLOCATION of the Cafeteria department (0220, «Employee Dining» in the ledger), whose cost is distributed by FTE. Computing it as a per diem on top of that would count it twice.

cargas_sociales_patronales.deDonde: Block C total: what the hotel pays on top of the wage.

ccss_patronal.deDonde: Employer Caja contribution on the taxable base. The engine calculates it when the scenario is recalculated; it is not keyed in.

ccssobrera.deDonde: Employee contribution: the percentage the hotel WITHHOLDS from the employee's gross wage and deposits with the CCSS. Classic pitfall: it is not a cost to the hotel — it comes out of the gross. The one the hotel pays ON TOP of the wage is the EMPLOYER contribution, and it is in block C.
ccssobrera.formula: gross × ccss_obrera_rate (10.67% = 5.50 SEM + 4.17 IVM + 1.00 Banco Popular)

cesantia_provision.deDonde: Severance accrual on the MONTH's taxable base. It builds up against the balance sheet and is paid out when the employee is settled on termination. If it comes out at zero, it has not been loaded: by law it runs 5.33%–8.33% a year.

costo_total_de_planilla_al_p_l.deDonde: The figure the P&L recognizes as payroll: the full 17 concepts. It has to match the block A total. Careful: it is already INSIDE the P&L cost that the cash flow pays — this table is informational and is not added a second time.
costo_total_de_planilla_al_p_l.formula: gross + employer contributions + benefits = Σ total_entry(e)

d_otros_beneficios.deDonde: Benefits in kind or in cash that do NOT contribute to the CCSS: they do not enter the taxable base, but they are hotel cost and they are cash.

e_resumen.deDonde: Rebuilds payroll cost starting from the gross, to show where every dollar of the figure that reaches the P&L comes from.

gastos_de_propiedad_ver_su_tab.deDonde: Rent + management fees + insurance + other below-GOP expenses, on ONE single line. It is grouped on purpose: the detail lives on its own tab, and breaking it out here as well reads as if the expense were counted twice (it is not).

incapacidades.deDonde: Sick-leave subsidy borne by the hotel (the portion the CCSS does not cover). It is manual: the user keys it in or it comes in through Excel, and the recalculation never overwrites it.

ins_riesgos_del_trabajo.deDonde: Workers' compensation policy (riesgos del trabajo), billed by the INS. It does not come from a per-person rate: the annual premium is loaded and the engine ALLOCATES it across the positions by FTE. A month with fewer people gets less.
ins_riesgos_del_trabajo.formula: c6022_occ_hazard — annual premium allocated by FTE

la_deduccion_obrera_se_retiene_y_se_remi.deDonde: Note. The hotel disburses the total cost: part of it to the employee and part to the CCSS. That is why the cash flow breaks out «net payroll» and «CCSS payment» on two separate lines.

movimiento_de_cuentas_por_pagar.deDonde: What is left owing (or gets finished off) during the month. It is read exactly as it stands from the accounts payable line of the Cash Flow Budget, whether it comes from the model, from a driver, from a manually overridden cell or from the actual Balance Sheet of a closed month.
movimiento_de_cuentas_por_pagar.formula: WC_AP from the indirect cash flow

nomina.deDonde: One row per department: the TOTAL payroll cost of that group, the sum of the 17 c60xx concepts of every position in the department for the month (wages, employer contributions and benefits, all together). Pitfall: allocation departments (Employee Dining, in-house laundry) do NOT show up here — their cost is distributed to the rest, so counting them would be double-counting.
nomina.formula: Σ total_entry(e) for e.dept_code ∈ group, e.month = m

opex.deDonde: One row per P&L expense line, departmental or overhead, on an accrual basis. Pitfall: when two codes share a name — «Laundry» the department and the house overhead — the house one is shown as «(overhead)» so the two do not get merged; one used to overwrite the other and the expense came out short.

otros.deDonde: Benefits that do not fall into the categories above. A monthly amount in colones per FTE.

otros_beneficios.deDonde: Block D total: cafeteria, transport, housing and other. They are not contributory, but they are cost.

pago_total_del_mes_sin_iva.deDonde: The month's real disbursement: the accrued cost less what is left to pay. It works out to paying a % in the month and the rest the following month, but carrying the tail from the prior year — January pays the balance of last December's invoice, which the old model skipped and is why January was off by $285,652.
pago_total_del_mes_sin_iva.formula: payment = accrued cost − Δ accounts payable

planilla.deDonde: The share of the month's payment that belongs to payroll. PITFALL: it is not calculated on its own — the TOTAL payment is split according to payroll's weight with its own lag. That is deliberate: this way the pieces tie exactly even when the movement comes from the actual balance sheet. Splitting by the current month's weight would come out wrong, because payroll is flat and expense is seasonal.
planilla.formula: payment × plan_ef / tot_ef, where ef = ap% × month + (1−ap%) × prior month

planilla_neta_a_pagar_al_empleado.deDonde: What actually gets deposited to the employee: the gross less the two withholdings. Old pitfall: this net used to be derived by subtracting the EMPLOYER CCSS from the wage — money the hotel pays ON TOP of the wage and never deducts from anyone — which left the net running about $457,000 a year below the real figure.

proveedores.deDonde: The rest of the month's payment: supplies, services, and the property expenses too, which run on this same schedule.

retencion_de_renta_al_salario_por_tramos.deDonde: Salary income tax that the hotel withholds from the employee and remits to the tax authority. It is NOT a flat percentage: it is progressive by bracket and computed person by person and month by month, with that month's exchange rate because the brackets are set in colones. In Budget 2027 only 5 of 122 employees fall into a taxable bracket.
retencion_de_renta_al_salario_por_tramos.formula: Σ retencion_persona(calc_base, tc_mes, tramos) — same calculation as the Taxes tab

salario_bruto.deDonde: The taxable base again, as the starting point of the summary: it is where the cost starts from, not the cost itself.
salario_bruto.formula: calc_base = the 7 concepts subject to contributions

salario_bruto_2.deDonde: Check figure: the three destinations have to add up to exactly the gross. If it does not tie, one of the withholdings is being calculated wrong.

salario_bruto_base_imponible.deDonde: This is the TAXABLE BASE, not the total cost: the 7 concepts subject to contributions — wages, overtime, day off, working holiday, commissions, vacation taken and bonus. CCSS and the Christmas bonus are calculated on this figure.

total_beneficios.deDonde: Sum of block D. None of it is contributory, so it does not affect the taxable base, the CCSS or the Christmas bonus.

total_cargas_sociales.deDonde: Sum of block C. It is the employer's surcharge on top of the wage; in Costa Rica it runs around a third of the gross. Note: that third is THIS block only; the total labour burden on salary — benefits included — runs considerably higher.
total_cargas_sociales.formula: ccss_pat + ins + Christmas bonus + vacation + severance + disabilities

total_costo_de_planilla.deDonde: Sum of every department: the 17 concepts of the 122 positions. It has to come out equal to «COSTO TOTAL DE PLANILLA (al P&L)» (total payroll cost to the P&L) in block E — it is the same money, one view by department and the other by concept.
total_costo_de_planilla.formula: Σ total_entry(e) over all positions × month

total_costo_devengado.deDonde: The month's cost according to the P&L. PITFALL: it is not the sum of the lines above, these are the P&L TOTALS. The engine emits each line under its canonical code and under an alias, so adding up the individual lines would double-count. It includes payroll in full. It is exactly the same expense base the indirect cash flow uses.

total_deducciones_al_empleado.deDonde: Both withholdings together: employee CCSS + salary income tax. This is the money the hotel deducts from the gross and remits on the employee's behalf.

total_pagado_sin_iva.deDonde: The month's disbursement for operating expense, excluding IVA. In the Summary this total comes out broken into net payroll, CCSS, Christmas bonus and suppliers, with IVA added on top.

transporte.deDonde: Staff transport allowance. A monthly amount in colones per FTE, converted at the month's exchange rate.

vacaciones_provision.deDonde: Vacation accrual on the month's taxable base. It builds up against the balance sheet: when the employee goes on vacation, the payment comes through as «vacation taken», which is contributory and is cash.

vivienda.deDonde: Staff housing, which matters at the lodge. A monthly amount in colones per FTE, converted at the month's exchange rate.

a_declarar_este_mes_nunca_negativo.deDonde: The tax declared for the month, already netted against the credit balance carried forward. It never drops below zero: if the result is in your favor, the return is zero and the difference goes to the credit.
a_declarar_este_mes_nunca_negativo.formula: to_declare = max(0, liability − accumulated credit balance)

a_gastos_de_propiedad_devengados_below_g.deDonde: The expenses that sit below the GOP line: they are not hotel operations, they belong to the owner of the building and to the management contract. They come off the P&L exactly as they are.

a_iva_del_mes_devengado.deDonde: The month's IVA on an ACCRUAL basis, not on what was collected: 13% on the P&L revenue and 13% on the P&L cost. This is the month's return, it is not cash that has gone out yet.

ajuste_al_movimiento_real.deDonde: The block C adjustment with the sign flipped, so that the total ends up being exactly the cash movement from the other screen.

ajuste_al_movimiento_real_de_la_otra_pan.deDonde: The difference between this tab and the IVA item in the indirect method. With the model as the source it is zero; it moves off when the month is closed with the actual balance sheet or when the cell has been overwritten by hand. This is the line that keeps the two methods tied.

alquiler.deDonde: Rent on the building. It is a monthly accrual; payment follows the supplier calendar like any other invoice.

b_auxiliar_del_saldo_a_favor.deDonde: The IVA trap in Costa Rica: when the month's position comes out in your favor, the tax authority does NOT refund the money. The credit is carried forward and applied against the following months' tax until it is used up. This subledger tracks that balance and always ties.

b_como_se_pagan.deDonde: All of these expenses follow the SAME payment criterion as the rest of the suppliers. Each one used to have its own rule here —the fee one month in arrears, the insurance semiannual— and a different one in the indirect method, for the very same expense.

c_inversion.deDonde: CapEx is kept apart from expense: it does not run through the result, and in the cash flow it drops down on its own line, after operating cash flow.

c_liquidacion.deDonde: From the return to the payment: what is declared this month, what is remitted out of what was declared last month, and what the net effect on cash is.

capex_del_presupuesto_del_p_l.deDonde: The CapEx line exactly as loaded in the scenario's P&L. It goes out in the month it is budgeted, with no lag: it does not enter the A/P calendar. For CapEx that is not in the budget, use the manual block below.

cobro_a_clientes_con_iva_neto_de_retenci.deDonde: It starts from the month's accrued revenue and moves it to the month the money comes in: deposits received for future stays are added, the ones applied to this month's stay are subtracted, and it is adjusted for the movement in A/R. On top goes the invoiced IVA, and the card withholdings are deducted (2.5% IVA + 2.5% income tax): those are not a payment made by the hotel, they are money that simply never arrives because the acquirer keeps it at settlement.
cobro_a_clientes_con_iva_neto_de_retenci.formula: TOTAL_REVENUES + deposits received + deposits applied + Δ A/R + IVA − withholdings

credito_aplicado_contra_el_impuesto.deDonde: How much of the credit balance was consumed to bring down the month's tax. It is the only way to recover the credit: by applying it, never by collecting it.

credito_generado_en_el_mes.deDonde: What the month added to the credit balance because the IVA paid plus the card withholding came out above the IVA charged. It happens in low season and in the months with the lodge closed.

d_lo_que_baja_al_flujo.deDonde: The Summary does not carry six tax lines: the reconciliation lives here and only ONE line drops down out of this whole tab.

e_memo_el_iva_que_viaja_dentro_de_otras_.deDonde: Memo, it does not add into the total. In reality IVA never moves on its own: it travels inside the customer collection and inside the supplier payment. It is shown here on its own so that it can be audited.

efecto_neto_del_iva_en_caja.deDonde: The cash impact of the month's IVA: the IVA on sales comes in, the IVA on purchases and the card withholding go out, and what was declared last month is remitted.
efecto_neto_del_iva_en_caja.formula: WC_TAX = the month's liability − the previous month's to_declare

el_iva_cobrado_va_dentro_de_cobro_a_clie.deDonde: The guest pays you the invoice with IVA included, so this amount is already inside customer collections in the Summary. Counting it again would double it.

el_iva_pagado_va_dentro_de_pago_a_provee.deDonde: You pay the supplier the invoice with IVA on it, so this amount is already inside the supplier payment in the Summary.

entradas_de_efectivo.deDonde: All the money that actually comes into the hotel's account during the month: what is collected from the guest and from the agencies (with IVA, already net of the withholdings the acquirer deducts) plus the F&B service charge 10%. Careful: what is shown here is the COLLECTION, not the sale — guests leave deposits months before the stay, so the two almost never fall in the same month.
entradas_de_efectivo.formula: customer collections + F&B service charge 10% F&B

entran_al_mismo_calendario_de_proveedore.deDonde: The same total from block A, shown here to make it explicit that it goes into the A/P pool.

honorarios_de_administracion.deDonde: Management fee and royalties. PITFALL: this takes the CALCULATED line from the P&L, not a % of sales rebuilt here. When the fee is entered by hand the percentage does not even apply — rebuilding it once made the very same item show $299,867 on one screen and $179,920 on the other.

iva_cobrado_a_clientes.deDonde: The 13% you charge the guest on top of the sale. It comes from the month's accrued revenue, not from the collection: it is declared with the invoice even if the guest has not paid yet.

iva_pagado_a_proveedores.deDonde: The 13% you paid on the month's purchases, which is credited against the 13% you charged. The base is the full P&L cost. If payroll were in-house it would carry no IVA and would be taken out of the base — that is governed by the «outsourced payroll» criterion.

las_dos_son_2_5_el_adquirente_las_descue.deDonde: A reading note: both withholdings carry the same rate, so they show the same amount every month and look like the same money counted twice. They are not: one is IVA and the other is income tax, two different taxes.

otros_gastos.deDonde: The rest of the below-GOP block: everything the P&L recognizes between GOP and EBITDA that is not rent, fees or insurance.

pago_a_la_ccss_cuota_patronal_obrera.deDonde: Both contributions together, because both are deposited with the CCSS on the same day: the employer share, which the hotel pays on top of the salary, and the employee share, which is withheld from the employee. It is kept in plain sight rather than hidden inside payroll because it is one of the largest disbursements of the month.
pago_a_la_ccss_cuota_patronal_obrera.formula: (employer CCSS + gross × employee rate) on the supplier calendar

pago_de_aguinaldo_se_provisiona_y_sale_e.deDonde: The Christmas bonus is accrued every month against the balance sheet, but it leaves cash only once, in its payment month. That is why each month's payroll payment comes reduced by the accrual and the outflow shows up here on its own. The annual total is the same: what is subtracted month by month is what goes out in one shot at the end.

pago_de_planilla_neta_a_empleados.deDonde: The share of the month's payment that belongs to payroll, shown the way it reaches the employee: without the CCSS (which has its own line) and without the Christmas bonus accrual (Costa Rica's statutory 13th-month bonus — that money does not go out this month). The split between payroll and suppliers is made on the TOTAL payment, respecting the lag of each one: splitting it by the weight of the current month would come out wrong, because payroll is flat and expenses are seasonal.
pago_de_planilla_neta_a_empleados.formula: (total payment × payroll weight + payroll IVA − Christmas bonus accrual) − CCSS payment

posicion_del_mes_debito_credito.deDonde: The month's position before touching the credit balance carried forward. Positive: you owe tax. Negative: you generated a credit.
posicion_del_mes_debito_credito.formula: liability = IVA charged − IVA paid − card withholding

remesa_a_hacienda_de_lo_declarado_el_mes.deDonde: The money you actually hand over to the tax authority this month: it is what was declared the PREVIOUS month. January pays December of last year — the model runs on a three-year window precisely so that it does not start from zero.

remesa_de_iva_a_hacienda.deDonde: The same remittance from block C, repeated here so you can see how the single line that drops into the Summary is put together.

remesa_de_iva_una_linea_en_el_resumen.deDonde: The only thing that is actually paid to the tax authority for IVA in the month. The card withholdings are NOT here: they are not payments made by the hotel, they come netted out of the collection.

retencion_de_iva_de_tarjeta.deDonde: The acquirer withholds 2.5% of IVA on everything you collect by card and remits it to the tax authority itself. It is not a payment you make: it is money that never reaches you, and that is why it reduces the month's liability.

retencion_de_iva_de_tarjeta_va_neta_del_.deDonde: The 2.5% of IVA the acquirer deducts from you when it settles the card. It is already subtracted from customer collections: you collect 97.5%, not 100%.

retencion_de_renta_de_tarjeta_va_neta_de.deDonde: The other 2.5%, this one on account of income tax. It also comes netted out of the collection, but it does not belong to IVA: it is an advance that is credited in the annual settlement (see the «Annual income tax» sub-tab).

saldo_a_favor_final.deDonde: The credit still alive at the close of the month, which travels on to the next one. The «Year» column shows December's, which is the one you carry into next year.
saldo_a_favor_final.formula: closing_balance = max(0, opening_balance − the month's liability)

saldo_inicial_viene_del_mes_anterior.deDonde: The credit balance the month starts with. The «Year» column does not add up the twelve months —a balance is not additive— it shows January's.

salidas_de_efectivo.deDonde: Everything that leaves the account during the month. It is not the accrued expense from the P&L: it is the expense already shifted to the month it is paid, on the same A/P calendar the Cash Flow Budget uses.

se_ven_dentro_de_pago_a_proveedores_y_pl.deDonde: A note. It tells you where to look for the cash outflow: there is no «property expense payment» line in the Summary because it sits inside the supplier payment.

seguros_de_la_propiedad.deDonde: The policy on the building. This is not the INS workers' compensation premium, which is payroll and lives in the Payroll tab. It is paid on the supplier calendar — it no longer has a semiannual rule of its own, which was one of the reasons the two methods did not tie.

servicio_10_a_b_cobrado_al_huesped.deDonde: The statutory F&B service charge 10% sales. It is charged to the guest along with the bill, but it is NOT hotel revenue: it is the employees' money passing through the till. That is why it comes in here and goes out on its own line the following month. Showing it net turned it negative in the months when F&B drops, and 10% of a sale cannot be negative. NEW PITFALL: the base is ONLY REV_FB. The Private Bar (dept 0121) came out of the F&B group and has its own revenue line (REV_PRIVATE_BAR), so its sales do NOT carry the 10%. Today this changes no number because that line is at zero; if Private Bar consumption should indeed carry the statutory service charge, the base has to be widened, and that is an owner's criterion, not a default.
servicio_10_a_b_cobrado_al_huesped.formula: 10% × REV_FB from the P&L (does not include REV_PRIVATE_BAR)

total_entradas.deDonde: Everything that came into cash during the month: the operating collections, the IVA that travels inside those collections and the F&B F&B service charge 10%, less the card withholdings.
total_entradas.formula: operating collections + IVA charged + F&B service charge 10% − card withholdings

total_gastos_de_propiedad.deDonde: Sum of block A. This total is already INSIDE the accrued cost on the Suppliers tab: it is not paid separately and must not be counted twice.

total_propiedad_inversion.deDonde: A control view of the below-GOP block plus investment. In the cash flow each piece drops down its own way —the expenses inside the supplier payment, the CapEx on its own line— so this total is never subtracted as such.

a_venta_devengada_sin_iva.deDonde: Opens up the month's sales line by line, exactly as they come out of the P&L and excluding IVA. This is ACCRUAL: it is the sales of the month, not what was collected. The conversion from sale to collection is in block C.

ajustes_manuales.deDonde: Cash in and cash out that fits on no other row. Useful for tying out to a bank statement, or for slipping in a one-off movement without touching the model.

b_iva_cobrado_13.deDonde: The IVA billed to the guest, broken out by the same revenue line. It is money that comes into the hotel's cash but is not the hotel's: it is owed to the tax authority and remitted the following month.

c_de_la_venta_al_cobro.deDonde: The bridge between what was sold and what was actually collected. At a lodge the guest leaves deposits months before the stay and sometimes a balance is left on credit afterwards, so the month of the sale and the month of the collection are almost never the same. These four pieces add up to exactly the operating collections. WATCH OUT: the collection criterion is NOT set per revenue line. The timing matrix and the card % are applied to the TOTAL of the sale, so every new line —the Private Bar, for instance— is collected on the same calendar as the rooms. There is no per-line entry that can be forgotten, but neither can a line be given payment terms of its own without changing the model.
c_de_la_venta_al_cobro.formula: sale + deposits received − deposits applied ± accounts receivable

cobro_operativo.deDonde: The money that actually comes in from the sale, excluding IVA and excluding the A&B service charge. It is the month's sales already shifted onto the real collection calendar.
cobro_operativo.formula: TOTAL_REVENUES + deposits received + deposits applied + Δ A/R

d_otros_cobros.deDonde: What comes into cash on top of the sale: the IVA billed and the 10% A&B service charge. Neither one is hotel revenue —one is owed to the tax authority and the other to the employees— but both pass through the bank account.

depositos_aplicados_a_la_estadia_del_mes.deDonde: The part of this month's sale that had ALREADY been collected earlier, as a deposit. It is subtracted because no new money comes in: that cash arrived in earlier months and here it is only drawn down against the stay.
depositos_aplicados_a_la_estadia_del_mes.formula: WC_DEP_APPL of the Cash Flow Budget

depositos_recibidos_por_estadias_futuras.deDonde: The advance payments that came in THIS month for stays that will happen later. How much, and how far in advance, is set by the collection matrix in the Criteria (from four months before to one month after). It is cash coming in today for a sale that has not been booked yet.
depositos_recibidos_por_estadias_futuras.formula: WC_DEP_RECV of the Cash Flow Budget

distribuciones_retiros.deDonde: Manual cell. Money paid out to the partners. It is not an expense, which is why it does not appear in the P&L, but it leaves the bank all the same.

flujo_neto_total.deDonde: How much the cash actually grew or shrank during the month, with everything in: the operation, the budgeted CapEx and the three manual blocks. It is the number that carries the balance from one month into the next.
flujo_neto_total.formula: operating cash flow − CapEx − capital − financing − adjustments

flujo_operativo.deDonde: The cash the operation left behind, before investment, loans and manual adjustments. It has to come out exactly the same as the indirect method: since both sides are built from the same series, Collections − Payments ≡ NOI + Δ Working Capital. If there is a difference, it is in the manual rows of one of the two screens.

impuesto_de_renta_liquidacion_sale_una_v.deDonde: The income tax, which leaves cash one single time, in its payment month (March by default). Do not confuse it with the advance payment: the 2.5% withheld on card collections is already deducted above, inside the collections from customers, and is credited against this settlement. The amount is entered by hand in the Taxes tab.
impuesto_de_renta_liquidacion_sale_una_v.formula: OTH_RENTA row of the Cash Flow Budget

informativo_financiamiento_requerido.deDonde: How much money you would have to raise that month to keep the balance out of the red. It is a warning: it is NOT added to the flow or to the balance. If this row has figures, the scenario needs financing and it has to be entered in the manual loans block.

intereses.deDonde: Manual cell. The interest actually paid during the month. Watch out for double counting: if the interest is already booked as a below-GOP expense in the P&L, it has already gone out inside the payment to suppliers.

inversion.deDonde: The investment in assets already budgeted inside the P&L. It is kept apart from operating cash flow because it is not an expense of the period: it is money that turns into an asset.

inversion_capex_adicional.deDonde: Manual cell. Investment in assets that never made it into the P&L. Careful with double counting: if it is already in the CapEx row above, do not repeat it here.

inversion_de_capital_adicional_manual.deDonde: Manual entry block: investment that is NOT in the P&L and still moves cash. None of this comes out of a calculation, and it is one of the few things that can make this cash flow differ from the indirect one.

iva_cobrado_a_clientes_2.deDonde: The same total as block B, repeated so you can see that the IVA comes into cash together with the collection. It sits in the bank until it is remitted the following month.

movimiento_de_cuentas_por_cobrar.deDonde: What is invoiced on credit and collected the following month, typically travel agencies. It adds when last month's invoices are collected and subtracts when new credit is granted.
movimiento_de_cuentas_por_cobrar.formula: WC_AR of the Cash Flow Budget

otra_inversion_de_capital.deDonde: Manual cell, a catch-all for any capital outflow that does not fit the two above: buying land, a contribution to a project.

otras_entradas_manuales.deDonde: Manual cell. Money that comes in and is neither from the operation nor from a loan: a refund, the sale of an asset, a one-off contribution.

otras_salidas_manuales.deDonde: Manual cell. Before using it, check whether the movement should really go under «Other Cash Movements» in the Cash Flow Budget: entered there it shows up in both methods, entered here it shows up only in this one.

otros_movimientos_de_caja.deDonde: Everything that falls under «Other Cash Movements» in the Cash Flow Budget and has no row of its own here. The income tax line is taken out of it, because it goes out on its own row and would otherwise be counted twice.
otros_movimientos_de_caja.formula: «Other Cash Movements» section of the indirect method, without OTH_RENTA

pago_a_proveedores_con_iva.deDonde: The month's accrued cost —OPEX, overhead and the below-GOP expenses— less whatever is still unpaid, plus the IVA on those purchases, and net of the payroll share already shown above. The trap: it drags along the tail of the prior year, so January pays the outstanding piece of last December's invoice.
pago_a_proveedores_con_iva.formula: (accrued cost − Δ A/P) − payroll share + IVA credit

posicion_de_caja.deDonde: The bank balance rolling month by month. It is the only part of the table where the figures are BALANCES and not movements, so they are not added up.

prestamos_e_intereses_manual.deDonde: Manual block with the financing: what comes in from loans and what goes out as principal repayment, interest and distributions. The P&L feeds none of this.

prestamos_recibidos.deDonde: Manual cell. Loan disbursements that come INTO cash. It is the only row in the block that adds: enter it as a positive.

remesa_de_iva_a_hacienda_ver_tab_impuest.deDonde: The only IVA payment made to the tax authority: last month's return. It is never negative, because when the position ends up in your favour the credit is carried forward instead of refunded. What is NOT here: neither the IVA collected nor the IVA paid —those travel inside the collections and the payments— nor the card withholdings, which come netted out of the collections.
remesa_de_iva_a_hacienda_ver_tab_impuest.formula: IVA filed for the prior month − adjustment to the actual movement

reserva_de_reposicion_ff_e.deDonde: Manual cell. The FF&E replacement reserve, for when money is genuinely set aside. If in your books it is only an accrual and no cash is actually transferred, leave it at zero: what belongs here is cash movements, not provisions.

rev.deDonde: A revenue line of the P&L (Rooms, A&B, Private Bar, Spa, Tours…), month by month and excluding IVA. It comes straight from the scenario's P&L engine, grouped by account code and not by name: two different lines can carry the same name, and one used to overwrite the other's figure. The lines are picked up by PREFIX (REV_*), not from a hand-written list, so a new profit centre shows up on its own. Collections, on the other hand, are computed on the TOTAL of the sale — see «C. FROM SALE TO COLLECTION».

reviva.deDonde: The IVA on that revenue line, at 13%. It is a direct calculation on the accrued sale, there only to show where each piece of the total comes from.

saldo_final_de_caja.deDonde: The money in the bank at the close of the month. It can end up negative, and it is shown negative on purpose: a projected cash flow has to be able to show the hole. There used to be a row that injected cash so the balance would never drop below zero, and that hid the problem and broke the comparison with the other method. Under «Year» you see DECEMBER's balance.

saldo_inicial_de_caja.deDonde: The money in the bank at the start of the month. January's is the opening balance from the parameters; the rest carry over the previous month's ending balance. In the «Year» column you see JANUARY's, not the sum of the twelve — adding them up gave eighteen million when opening cash is two hundred and fifty thousand.
saldo_inicial_de_caja.formula: month 1 = opening_cash; month n = ending balance of month n−1

se_le_paga_a_los_empleados_el_mes_siguie.deDonde: The other side of the row above: the service charge collected in earlier months that is handed over to the employees. It is shown as a negative because it is a reminder of the outflow; the payment itself goes out on its own row in the Summary.

servicio_10_a_b_pagado_a_empleados.deDonde: The other side of the 10% charged to the guest: it is handed over to the employees with the lag set in the Criteria. It is backed out of the net movement of the Cash Flow Budget so that the cash effect is the same even when it comes from the actual Balance Sheet of a closed month.

servicio_de_deuda_amortizacion.deDonde: Manual cell. The principal portion of the instalments only. Interest goes on the row below, kept separate, because interest is an expense and principal repayment is not.

subtotal_ajustes.deDonde: The net of the two manual adjustments.

subtotal_capital.deDonde: The sum of the three manual capital cells. All three are cash out, so a positive number reduces the month's net flow.

subtotal_financiamiento.deDonde: The net effect of financing on the month's cash. If it comes out negative, financing put money into the month.
subtotal_financiamiento.formula: principal repayment + interest + distributions − loans received

total_entradas_de_caja.deDonde: Everything that came in during the month, and it is the same figure as the «TOTAL INFLOWS» of the Summary. The trap: it is not the visual sum of the rows above, because it also deducts the card withholdings —2.5% for IVA and 2.5% for income tax— which have no row of their own here. The acquirer keeps them at settlement, so it is money that never reaches the account.
total_entradas_de_caja.formula: operating collections + IVA + service charge − card withholdings

total_iva_cobrado.deDonde: The total IVA billed during the month. It comes from the calendar shared with the Cash Flow Budget, so it may not match the sum of the lines exactly if the P&L detail differs from the total. This is the figure that flows down into the cash flow, inside the collections from customers.

total_salidas_operativas.deDonde: Everything paid out during the month for the operation. It does not include investment or the manual capital and financing rows. The «− otros» in the formula is not a mistake: «other cash movements» is stored with an INFLOW sign, so subtracting it from outflows adds it to the flow. That is why the row is shown negated.
total_salidas_operativas.formula: payroll + CCSS + Christmas bonus + suppliers + service charge + IVA + income tax − other

total_venta_devengada.deDonde: Total sales for the month. It comes from the P&L total —not from adding up the lines above— so that the base of this method is identical to the Cash Flow Budget's. If it does not tie to the detail, the difference is in the P&L, not here.

venta_devengada_del_mes.deDonde: The starting point: total sales for the month according to the P&L. It is not money in the bank yet — the three lines below shift it to the month in which it is collected.

cfdAyuda.belowGopSinClasificar: Below-GOP expense the total includes but that is not stored as rent, management fee, insurance or «other». In scenarios with actual months the total is derived from GOP minus EBITDA Before, and that subtraction captures amounts never loaded under a line of their own. The total is right; what is missing is knowing what it is. If it ever gets classified, this row drops to zero on its own.
